games.title: The shot on f7 you missed four times
games.summary: Black jumped the knight into the center and later brought the bishop out toward your king. Each time, f7 was guarded only by the king and taking it with the bishop won a pawn and wrecked Black's king. The game was lost much later to a tactic on move 18.

games.title: Three chances to push the e-pawn
games.summary: Black stepped the bishop back, a line from your study. Your d-pawn push was fine (the engine even likes it a touch more), but three times the e-pawn push to kick the knight was the strongest move, and each time it was skipped.

games.title: The line your study doesn't cover
games.summary: Black declined your gambit pawn with the quiet d-pawn move, which isn't in your study. Later you missed taking the knight first, and taking on f7, before the long diagonal decided the game.

games.title: Black ignored f7 and paid for it
games.summary: Black attacked your bishop instead of defending f7. You grabbed the rook and won. The bishop capture on f7 is even cleaner; it's now in the guide.

games.title: Fried Liver, mate in 12
games.summary: The textbook Fried Liver. Black's king ran back home, you took the knight, and the king hunt ended in mate.

games.title: The f7 shot, in a different opening
games.summary: Black guarded the center pawn with the d-pawn and a knight, then spent a move on the h-pawn. Taking on f7 with the bishop was winning. The quiet bishop move let Black off, and the game was lost much later.

games.title: Push past the knight, twice
games.summary: The small pawn move and the big center, exactly right. Then Black's knight sat within reach of your d-pawn and pushing it was the best move, twice in a row. You won anyway, by checkmate.

games.title: A piece up, then one queen move
games.summary: Black left the bishop hanging on move five and you took it. You stayed a piece up for twelve more moves. Then your queen went to a square Black's knight covered.

games.title: The queen check you blocked with the queen
games.summary: Black's queen checked you on move three. Blocking with your queen traded queens and took away your lead in development; Black ground out a long ending.

games.title: Six moves: guard the e-pawn first
games.summary: Black's bishop and knight both hit your e-pawn. You moved your other bishop, lost the pawn, then a second pawn and the rook in the corner. Guard the pawn, or push it past the knight.
